dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Code on Wages, 2019
The Code on Wages, 2019 is a landmark reform in India's labour framework. It modernizes, simplifies, and consolidates multiple fragmented laws into a single, comprehensive regulation. 
1. Objectives of the Code
The primary objective of the Code on Wages is to establish uniformity, transparency, and accountability in the payment of wages and bonuses while fostering a progressive economic environment. Key aims include: 
•	Consolidation of Laws: Amalgamating 4 central labor legislations into a single code to eliminate multiplicity of definitions and authorities. 
•	Universal Wage Security: Extending the statutory right to minimum wages and timely payment protections to all employees across both the organized and unorganized sectors. 
•	Ease of Compliance: Simplifying regulatory procedures through technology (e.g., single filings, digital registries) to reduce compliance burdens for establishments. 
•	Removal of Disparities: Eradicating gender discrimination in recruitment and wage payments for work of similar nature. 
2. Laws Subsumed
The Code on Wages replaces the following four central acts: 
1.	The Payment of Wages Act, 1936
2.	The Minimum Wages Act, 1948
3.	The Payment of Bonus Act, 1965
4.	The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976
3. Key Provisions
A. Universal Coverage & Unified Definition of Wages
•	Universal Applicability: Unlike older laws that limited protections to specific wage ceilings or "scheduled employments," the Code covers all employees in both the public and private sectors. 
•	Standardized Wage Structure: Defines wages explicitly to comprise three core components: Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance (DA), and Retaining Allowance. 
o	The 50% Rule: If an employee's excluded components (such as house rent, conveyance, or other special allowances) exceed 50% (or any specified percentage) of their total remuneration, the excess amount is added back into the wage pool. This directly standardizes calculations for social security benefits like Provident Fund (PF) and Gratuity. 
B. National Floor Wage & Minimum Wages
•	Floor Wage: The Central Government is empowered to fix a National Floor Wage based on the living standards of workers. 
•	State Obligations: State governments cannot set minimum wage rates lower than the national floor wage. If a state's existing minimum wage is higher than the floor wage, it cannot be reduced. 
•	Revision Intervals: Minimum wages must be reviewed and revised by the appropriate government at least once every 5 years. 
•	Determinants: Minimum wage structures are fixed based on geographical areas, skill levels (unskilled, semi-skilled, skilled, highly skilled), and the arduousness/difficulty of the work. 
C. Timely Payment of Wages
The Code mandates strict timelines for wage clearance depending on the wage period: 
•	Daily / Shift-end: At the end of the shift or day. 
•	Weekly: Before the weekly holiday. 
•	Fortnightly: Within two days of the end of the fortnight. 
•	Monthly: Before the expiry of the 7th day of the succeeding month. 
•	Resignation / Termination: Wages must be settled within 2 working days of separation. 
•	Modes of Payment: Payments can be made in coins, currency notes, via cheque, or by direct digital credit to the employee’s bank account. 
D. Permissible Deductions
Employer deductions from an employee’s wage are restricted to specific categories (e.g., fines, absence from duty, damage to property, recovery of advances, or accommodation provided by the employer). Total deductions cannot exceed 50% of an employee’s total wages. 
E. Bonus Payments
•	Eligibility: Employees drawing wages below a specific notified monthly threshold and who have worked for at least 30 days in an accounting year are eligible for an annual bonus. 
•	Calculation: The minimum bonus is fixed at 8.33% of wages or ₹100, whichever is higher, scaling up to a maximum cap of 20% of annual wages. 
F. Gender Equality
•	The Code strictly prohibits gender-based discrimination in matters concerning wage payment, hiring, and conditions of employment for work of the same or similar nature (evaluated on parameters of skill, effort, experience, and responsibility). 
G. Enforcement, Penalties, and Dispute Resolution
•	Inspector-cum-Facilitators: Replaces traditional inspectors with "Inspectors-cum-Facilitators" who provide advisory support for compliance alongside enforcement capabilities.
•	Extended Limitation Period: The time limit for employees to file wage-related claims has been expanded to 3 years (up from previous limits ranging between 6 months to 2 years). 
•	Graded Penalties: Penalties are structured based on the gravity of the violation. For minor, first-time infractions not punishable by imprisonment, provisions for compounding (settling) offenses are emphasized over immediate criminal prosecution.

dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021
The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021 (Act No. 19 of 2021) – Brief Summary
The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021 was enacted to declare certain food technology institutes as Institutions of National Importance (INI) and to promote excellence in education, research, innovation, entrepreneurship, and skill development in the food processing sector. The Act came into force on 1 October 2021. 
Objectives
•	To establish world-class institutions for education and research in food technology, entrepreneurship, and management. 
•	To develop skilled professionals for the food processing industry. 
•	To promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and industry collaboration. 
•	To strengthen India's food processing sector through advanced research and technology. 
Key Provisions
•	Declares the following institutes as Institutions of National Importance: 
o	National Institute of Food Technology Entrepreneurship and Management (NIFTEM), Kundli, Haryana. 
o	Indian Institute of Food Processing Technology (IIFPT), Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu (now National Institute of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management–Thanjavur). 
•	Provides for the incorporation of these institutes as autonomous statutory bodies. 
•	Establishes governance through: 
o	Board of Governors, 
o	Senate, 
o	Director, 
o	Finance Committee, 
o	Building and Works Committee, and 
o	A Central Council for coordination among the institutes. 
•	Empowers the institutes to award degrees, diplomas, and other academic distinctions. 
•	Provides for Central Government funding, maintenance of institute funds, accounts, and audits. 
•	Authorizes the Central Government to make rules and the institutes to frame Statutes and Ordinances for administration. 
Significance
•	Enhances the quality of higher education and research in food technology. 
•	Supports the growth of India's food processing industry by producing skilled manpower. 
•	Encourages innovation, startup creation, and entrepreneurship in the agri-food sector. 
•	Strengthens India's competitiveness in food processing and contributes to food security and economic development

Legislative History: 
The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021

Source: India Code and Ministry of Food Processing Industries Official Records

Short Title - The National Institutes of Food Technology, Entrepreneurship and Management Act, 2021 
Act Number / Year - Act No. 19 of 2021
India Code Act ID - 202119
Introduced In -	Lok Sabha
Presidential Assent Date -July 30, 2021
Official Gazette Publication -July 30, 2021 
Enforcement Date - October 1, 2021 
 Nodal Ministry - Ministry of Food Processing Industries 

Precedent & Statutory Rationale
1.	Limitations of Society-Managed Status:
o	Prior to 2021, premier institutions dedicated to food science, technology, and management functioned under registered societies. This setup limited their institutional autonomy, financial flexibility, nationwide expansion, and ability to design dynamic global academic and research collaborations.
2.	Elevating Food Science and Processing to National Priorities:
o	Grounded in national economic objectives to strengthen the food processing sector, reduce post-harvest losses, promote value addition, and encourage entrepreneurship, the legislation was enacted to elevate key institutions to apex national standing, mirroring premier technical bodies like IITs.

Parliamentary Trajectory & Enactment
•	Formulation: Developed and piloted by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries under the Union Government to provide statutory backing, academic independence, and uniform governance standards to premier food technology institutes.
•	Parliamentary Passage: Introduced in Parliament, thoroughly debated, and passed by both Houses during the monsoon session of July 2021.
•	Presidential Assent: Received formal Presidential Assent on July 30, 2021, entering the statute book as Act No. 19 of 2021.
•	Enforcement: Brought into active operational force on October 1, 2021.

1.	Administration by Governor General in Council: - Exclusive authority to administer the King of Oudh's estate.
•	Power to settle claims, distribute remaining property/proceeds among the King's family and dependents as deemed fit.
•	Immunity: No act of the Governor General in Council regarding the estate's administration or distribution can be questioned in any Court.
2.	Indemnity: - The Agent to the Governor General and those acting under his orders are indemnified for all acts related to preserving and administering the estate since 20th September, 1887.
•	No suits can be instituted against them or the Secretary of State for India in Council regarding these acts.
3.	Effect of the Act: - Supersedes any testamentary disposition made by the late King.
•	Overrides any Civil Court proceedings for administering the estate or collecting debts.
•	Requires anyone who has received part of the estate under any probate to account for it to an appointed officer.

115A. Rights of victims and witnesses.--(1) It shall be the duty and responsibility of the State to make arrangements for the protection of victims, their dependents, and witnesses against any kind of intimidation or coercion or inducement or violence or threats of violence.
(2) A victim shall be treated with fairness, respect and dignity and with due regard to any special need that arises because of the victims age or gender or educational disadvantage or poverty.
(3) A victim or his dependent shall have the right to reasonable, accurate, and timely notice of any Court proceeding including any bail proceeding and the Special Public Prosecutor or the State Government shall inform the victim about any proceedings under this Act.
(4) A victim or his dependent shall have the right to apply to the Special Court or the Exclusive Special Court, as the case may be, to summon parties for production of any documents or material, witnesses or examine the persons present.
(5) A victim or his dependent shall be entitled to be heard at any proceeding under this Act in respect of bail, discharge, release, parole, conviction or sentence of an accused or any connected proceedings or arguments and file written submission on conviction, acquittal or sentencing.
(6) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Code of Criminal Procedure,1973 (2 of 1974), the Special Court or the Exclusive Special Court trying a case under this Act shall provide to a victim, his dependent, informant or witnesses--
(a) the complete protection to secure the ends of justice;
(b) the travelling and maintenance expenses during investigation, inquiry and trial;
(c) the social-economic rehabilitation during investigation, inquiry and trial; and
(d) relocation.
(7) The State shall inform the concerned Special Court or the Exclusive Special Court about the protection provided to any victim or his dependent, informant or witnesses and such Court shall periodically review the protection being offered and pass appropriate orders.
(8) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-section (6), the concerned Special Court or the Exclusive Special Court may, on an application made by a victim or his dependent, informant or witness in any proceedings before it or by the Special Public Prosecutor in relation to such victim, informant or witness or on its own motion, take such measures including--
(a) concealing the names and addresses of the witnesses in its orders or judgments or in any records of the case accessible to the public;
(b) issuing directions for non-disclosure of the identity and addresses of the witnesses;
(c) take immediate action in respect of any complaint relating to harassment of a victim, informant or witness and on the same day, if necessary, pass appropriate orders for protection:
Provided that inquiry or investigation into the complaint received under clause (c) shall be tried separately from the main case by such Court and concluded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of the complaint:
Provided further that where the complaint under clause (c) is against any public servant, the Court shall restrain such public servant from interfering with the victim, informant or witness, as the case may be, in any matter related or unrelated to the pending case, except with the permission of the Court.
(9) It shall be the duty of the Investigating Officer and the Station House Officer to record the complaint of victim, informant or witnesses against any kind of intimidation, coercion or inducement or violence or threats of violence, whether given orally or in writing, and a photocopy of the First Information Report shall be immediately given to them at free of cost.
(10) All proceedings relating to offences under this Act shall be video recorded.
(11) It shall be the duty of the concerned State to specify an appropriate scheme to ensure implementation of the following rights and entitlements of victims and witnesses in accessing justice so as--
(a) to provide a copy of the recorded First Information Report at free of cost;
(b) to provide immediate relief in cash or in kind to atrocity victims or their dependents;
(c) to provide necessary protection to the atrocity victims or their dependents, and witnesses;
(d) to provide relief in respect of death or injury or damage to property;
(e) to arrange food or water or clothing or shelter or medical aid or transport facilities or daily allowances to victims;
(f) to provide the maintenance expenses to the atrocity victims and their dependents;
(g) to provide the information about the rights of atrocity victims at the time of making complaints and registering the First Information Report;
(h) to provide the protection to atrocity victims or their dependents and witnesses from intimidation and harassment;
(i) to provide the information to atrocity victims or their dependents or associated organisations or individuals, on the status of investigation and charge sheet and to provide copy of the charge sheet at free of cost;
(j) to take necessary precautions at the time of medical examination;
(k) to provide information to atrocity victims or their dependents or associated organisations or individuals, regarding the relief amount;
(l) to provide information to atrocity victims or their dependents or associated organisations or individuals, in advance about the dates and place of investigation and trial;
(m) to give adequate briefing on the case and preparation for trial to atrocity victims or their dependents or associated organisations or individuals and to provide the legal aid for the said purpose;
(n) to execute the rights of atrocity victims or their dependents or associated organisations or individuals at every stage of the proceedings under this Act and to provide the necessary assistance for the execution of the rights.
(12) It shall be the right of the atrocity victims or their dependents, to take assistance from the NonGovernment Organisations, social workers or advocates.]
